edit.description: Retire the advisory and the segment model behind it: `UNMODELED_RULE` (:31), step (2)'s whole `KNOWN_SURFACES` loop (:122-:171) with both verdict branches (`SegmentCoverage::Partial`, `SegmentCoverage::Wholly`), and the machinery only that loop reaches — `present` (:250), `governed_by_any` (:261), `governs_segment` (:311), `SegmentCoverage` (:321), `manifest_top_level_keys` (:346), `segment_coverage` (:364), `verb` (:404) — plus the unit tests driving them (:546, :565, :583, :630, :657, :682, :730). What survives is the disclosure note (1) and the unclaimed-entry scan (3) with `with_locked_kinds` (:234), `governed_by_any_path`, `governs` and its helpers; the governance unit tests that still earn their keep re-point at `governed_by_any_path`. The module header's opening paragraph states the surviving two finding classes.

`KNOWN_SURFACES` shrinks to the unclaimed-entry exclusion list: the `.mcp.json` row goes (the scan walks `.claude/` only, so a row outside it excludes nothing), `Segment` (:63) and the `segments` column go with the advisory, and every `KnownSurface` column the exclusion test does not read — `is_dir`, `holds`, `source`, and `SETTINGS_DOC` if it loses its last reader — goes with them. The module header (:11-:14) names the registry's one surviving job.

The doc comment at :301 promises that a governing kind 'retires its host file's `coverage.unmodeled-surface` finding' — the finding no longer exists, so the sentence states what governance actually buys now.

The integration suite's advisory cases retire: the partial-governance case (:106-:145), the fully-represented case (:213), the only-modeled-surfaces case (:256), and the `.mcp.json` arms (:318, :345, :370, :399) — including the two that withhold a built-in from the kind set to observe the advisory at all, the fixtures decision 0071 retires with the rule. The disclosure-note cases and the four unclaimed-entry cases stay, and the file's header states the two classes it still covers.

The suppression case at :491 asserts a `coverage.unmodeled-surface` finding for `.claude/settings.json` with the container withheld — it retires with the rule; keep whatever cost assertion the case carries beside it by re-pointing at a surviving finding class.

The two advisory-retirement cases (:265, :302-:308) assert the absence of a finding class that no longer exists — vacuous once the rule is gone, so they retire, and the file header's claim (:14) drops with them. The rollup-fingerprint and undeclared-member halves of the same narrative stay.
The case reading `coverage.unmodeled-surface` at :427 states what still holds — the hook's segment is checked beside the container's member — without naming the retired rule.

summary: `coverage.unmodeled-surface` retires with the segment model behind it: both config files are governed whole, so the advisory has no subject left to name.

tests.asserts: the coverage note reports exactly two classes — the checked disclosure and the unclaimed `.claude/` entry — and no run names an unmodeled surface
the note's cost claim holds against a surviving finding class, with no fixture withholding a built-in kind

acceptance: cargo test green with no test withholding a built-in kind to observe a finding, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean (no dead code behind the retired rule), cargo fmt --all --check clean.
notes: Decision 0071's retirement half — the subject is gone once `mcp` governs `.mcp.json` whole, which is why this waits on that entry rather than shipping beside it. Symbol-scope blast radius: the census above is the whole `rg unmodeled` set outside `specs/decisions/`. Blocked on DIRECTIVE-BACKING-RESOLVES-BY-STAT for tests/it/check_cost.rs alone. Invariant 6 is served by the kinds now: every key reaches a row. scoped at 3070b747
